neighbours.label: the punctuation closing a short exclamatory or rhetorical fragment ('What?', a 'one X, one Y' slogan) that interrupts the text before an elaboration; weak guess
fire: The manager told us the office would close for a month. What? Nobody had warned the staff at all.
She read the letter twice and gasped. What? Her uncle had left the farm to a stranger.
The referee waved the goal away. What? Even the visiting fans could not believe it.
One country, one party, one leader, was the cry painted on the walls of the town.
My brother called to say he had sold the car. What? He had bought it only last week.
The waiter handed us the bill for ninety dollars. What? We had only ordered soup.
One team, one dream, one goal, read the banner hanging over the stadium gate.
The teacher said the exam had been moved to today. What? Half the class had not studied.
quiet: The manager told us the office would close for a month, and the staff began packing their desks.
She read the letter twice and smiled, because her uncle had sent a photo of the farm.
The referee waved the goal away and the game continued for ten more minutes.
The party chose a new leader in the spring and painted the town hall walls.
My brother called to say he had sold the car to a neighbour for a fair price.
The waiter handed us the bill and we paid it with cash at the door.
The team hung a large banner over the stadium gate before the match.
The teacher said the exam would be held on Thursday in the main hall.
